transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

A whistle or change in pitch usually means a part-blocked airway. Please switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. With the power safely disconnected, look through the hose, wand and floorhead neck and check the bin inlet for any obstructions. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is the hose split, or was it all clear?
I've unplugged it and looked. The hose is clear, as a coin dropped straight through it, and I can't see any split. The bag and filter are new too, so I don't think it is a blockage.

Thanks for confirming there are no blockages and the filters are seated. Please switch off and unplug your vacuum, or remove the battery if applicable, before proceeding. A rattle or click often indicates something caught in the floorhead. Turn the unit over to inspect it. 1. Remove any debris stuck inside. 2. Cut away tangled hair or fibres. 3. Check that the brush bar turns freely by hand. Was something caught (and is it clear now), is the bar broken, or was it clean and turning freely?

I'm afraid it's a cylinder vacuum with a brush-less hose and floorhead, so I'm not sure the floorhead is the problem. The rough sound comes from the motor itself, and the suction is weak at both the hose end and the head. Do you think the motor is the issue?

[Heading: Motor bearing or fan]
Thanks for letting me know about that grinding noise. Based on what you have shared, the motor bearing or fan is the most likely area involved, though I cannot confirm this from our current information. Please stop using the vacuum if it gets worse or smells hot; seeing a repairer is the next step, and I am not recommending any specific part based solely on the noise. If you haven’t had a chance yet, the check I described earlier comes first. To be safe, switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) before doing anything else.
Now that you mention a hot smell, it does give off a hot, burning electrical smell after about five minutes of running. Should I carry on using it, or is that a sign to stop?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using the machine, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't use it again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer.
